questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control airflow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed. This prevents air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Roll over less easily than empty rigs.
Roll over more easily than empty rigs.
Roll over just as easily as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roll over more easily than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs roll over more easily. The cargo weight raises the center of gravity, making the vehicle less stable.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause your trailer to skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes have no brakes if the air supply leaks because:

options.text: The trailer will have no working brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no working brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank leaks empty, there will be no brakes on the trailer. The wheels will spin freely.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May get extra support during turns.
May be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean during turns.
questions.explanation: A load on one side causes the trailer to lean that way. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: If you are backing and unsure of your path, you should:

options.text: Stop and get out to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure while backing, stop the vehicle. Get out and check your path before continuing.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.correctAnswerText: You turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers are caused by turning too fast. Drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when towing.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers attached.
questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a trailer attached. Bobtails take longer to stop than a loaded tractor and trailer combination.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows fuel level
A valve that limits cargo weight

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar is the trailer hand valve. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are harder to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or another vehicle.
Park it on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks.
questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent the trailer from moving.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies service lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Air lines are color-coded to help drivers connect them correctly. Blue is used for service lines. Red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands to each other.
Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Only connect one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands to each other.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: Place the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position to test:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start a trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then, pull out the trailer air supply control or place it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver should:

options.text: Not apply the trailer hand brake.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer begins to jackknife, release the brakes so the trailer wheels can grip the road again. Do not apply the trailer hand brake. Applying brakes is what caused the wheels to lock and jackknife in the first place.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Send air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the trailer air supply control to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and is connected to the ____ valves.
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is connected to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance can present problems when driving over:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Railroad-highway crossings can be difficult to cross when pulling a trailer with low underneath clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially challenging to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Loaded with most weight on the driver's side of the trailer.
Placed near the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread evenly throughout the trailer.
questions.explanation: Distribute cargo weight evenly inside the trailer to reduce the risk of a rollover. Do not put too much weight on one side of the trailer.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need extra space on the road because they:

options.text: Drive more slowly than other commercial vehicles.
Are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles. Managing space properly is especially important when operating a combination vehicle.
